init-easy-current-empty.label: Initialize the current folder
init-easy-current-empty.story: Your team has finally started its first project together. Raven, your group leader, has created the project folder, assigned the work, and confidently announced that everyone should “stay organized.” Ten minutes later, someone asks whether they should make a backup before editing, and another teammate suggests copying the folder every afternoon. Raven pauses. “Let’s avoid creating a museum of backup folders.” Nothing has been recorded yet, and the current folder has no version control. Before anyone starts changing files, the team needs a way to keep track of its work. You have been given the setup job; the first actual snapshot will come later.
init-easy-current-empty.starting_point: You are in an empty project folder. It is not a repository yet.
init-easy-current-empty.real_world_context: Teams often begin with an ordinary folder. Initializing it gives Git a place to record future snapshots, while the files remain unstaged until someone deliberately adds them.
init-easy-current-empty.task: Initialize the current directory as a Git repository with main as its initial branch. Do not stage files or create a commit.
objective_checks: A Git repository exists in the current folder.
The first branch is main.
Nothing is staged and no commit exists.
init-easy-current-empty.expected_result: The current folder is now a repository on main. It has no commits and nothing is staged.
accepted_alternatives: Pattern: `git init -b main`. Option order does not matter; `-b main` = `-bmain` = `--initial-branch=main` = `--initial-branch main`; the folder may be written `dir`, `./dir`, `dir/` or as an absolute path. Not accepted: `git init --bare`, a different branch name or capitalization (`Main`), initializing the parent folder, staging or committing files.

Bare `git init` is accepted when the simulator's default first branch is `main` (the end state is identical). A hint should tell the learner that real Git may start on another name and that `-b main` removes the doubt.
Common patterns that apply: P19.
evaluation: Repository at `.`; HEAD on `main`; 0 commits; nothing staged.

init-easy-trunk-branch.label: Initialize with trunk as the first branch
init-easy-trunk-branch.story: It’s your first morning at a software company, and Sage is helping you prepare your workspace. The onboarding guide looks straightforward until you notice that the team calls its main development line trunk. You ask whether that is a typo. “Nope. Someone picked the tree metaphor years ago, and now we’re committed,” Sage says, pointing to the same name in the build instructions and team handbook. Your current project folder is still outside version control. Before development begins, its setup needs to match the team’s naming convention. Sage promises the rest of onboarding involves fewer trees, although you haven’t reached the branching discussion yet.
init-easy-trunk-branch.starting_point: You are in an empty project folder. It is not a repository yet.
init-easy-trunk-branch.real_world_context: Branch names appear in build scripts, review instructions, and teammate habits. Starting this repository on trunk avoids a naming mismatch before work begins.
init-easy-trunk-branch.task: Initialize the current directory as a Git repository with trunk as its initial branch.
objective_checks: A Git repository exists in the current folder.
The first branch is trunk.
init-easy-trunk-branch.expected_result: The current folder is now a repository on trunk.
accepted_alternatives: Pattern: `git init -b trunk`. Option order does not matter; `-b main` = `-bmain` = `--initial-branch=main` = `--initial-branch main`; the folder may be written `dir`, `./dir`, `dir/` or as an absolute path. Not accepted: `git init --bare`, a different branch name or capitalization (`Main`), initializing the parent folder, staging or committing files.

Two commands: `git init`, then a branch rename inside the new repository (`git branch -m trunk`, `git branch -M trunk`, `git branch --move trunk`, `git switch -c trunk`, `git checkout -b trunk`); accepted, not CAR-accurate. The simulator must support renaming a branch that has no commits.
Common patterns that apply: P19.
evaluation: Repository at `.`; HEAD on `trunk`; 0 commits.
